title: Regular Expression Matching
summary: Given an input string and a pattern, implement matching for regular expressions that include '.' and '*', where '.' matches any single character and '*' matches zero or more of the preceding character.
statement: Given an input string and a pattern, implement matching for regular expressions that include '.' and '*', where '.' matches any single character and '*' matches zero or more of the preceding character. Return true if the pattern matches the entire string.
constraints: s and p each have length 1–20. s contains lowercase English letters.
p contains lowercase letters, '.' (one arbitrary character), and '*' (zero or more of the preceding atom).
Every star follows a valid non-star atom. Match the entire string, not a substring.
hints: A star belongs to the atom before it; this differs from an independent wildcard star.
Define whether each text prefix matches each pattern prefix.
For x*, either skip both pattern characters or consume a matching text character while retaining x*. An ordinary atom consumes one from both sides.
Initialize empty-text matches through chains of starred atoms, then return the full-prefix state.
editorial: Use prefix DP. An ordinary letter or dot needs the preceding text/pattern prefixes to match and then consumes one character. A starred atom has two choices: zero repetitions drops that atom and its star, while another matching repetition consumes a text character without advancing the pattern. Only the previous text row and the current row are needed. This avoids exponential recursive re-exploration; memoized recursion is an equivalent formulation. The independent oracle uses Python's full-match regex engine on exactly this restricted grammar.

tests.explanation: The pattern consumes only one a, so it does not cover the entire two-character input.
Use zero copies of c, two copies of a, then b; the full string matches.
